1.explanation: 1) packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js contains the classNames and markup for the React <Tabs> component. To support a secondary style, we must add a new prop and toggle an extra modifier class here.  2) packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-story.js is the Storybook demo for React Tabs; it needs a new story or knob to surface the secondary variation.  3) packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.js is the core vanilla-JS implementation that applies CSS classes (e.g. selectorButtonSelected, classActive); to get the secondary design at runtime, its class list and _updateMenuState logic will need to conditionally emit a new modifier class on the container and tabs.  4) packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.config.js drives the static HTML/CSS variant in the style system; adding a “secondary” variant here ensures Sketch/templating and the style guide publish the new look.
1.bug_scenario: The customer wants a “secondary” Tabs style in addition to the default. In the screenshot, the active tab (“Application Discovery”) appears with a blue type color and underline on a white background, while inactive tabs have light grey backgrounds and grey text. They’d like to add a new prop (e.g. secondary) to the React <Tabs> component and a corresponding CSS variant in the vanilla JS Tabs so that authors can opt into this alternate look.
